newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi of America personnel manager resigns.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi of America personnel manager resigns.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America Inc said Monday its personnel manager had resigned, five months after the carmaker was sued by a federal agency for alleged sexual harassment of workers.
The company, a unit of Mitsubishi Motors Corp, said Patrick Walter, who was hired for the Normal plant in 1986, had chosen to "pursue personal goals."

The U.S. Equal Opportunity Commission filed a federal lawsuit against Mitsubishi April 9 in Peoria, Ill., alleging that as many as 700 female employees at the plant were subject to sexual harrassment by male employees and could be eligible for compensatory and punitive damages of $300,000 each.
Mitsubishi has denied the charges but hired former Labor Secretary Lynn Martin to address employment and training issues and set up a seperate Office of Opportunity Programs.

To replace Walter on an interim basis when he leaves October 1, the company said Osamu Ito will become general manager of the department. Ito was scheduled to become an executive vice president in charge of human resources at the end of September.
